description:
Two different closures passed through a helper into one shared function fail to compile on all three paths. A single closure works, and calling `f.()` directly in the helper works. Predates the epic: same failure on the base binary at 6ac603ac5. The distiller hits it through Enum.max/min with a fallback (distill lines 278, 279, 286, 298), so it blocks the Enum ticket.

Reproduce (scratchpad sc813/min.fz):

    defp ext([], f), do: f.()
    defp ext([h | _], _f), do: h
    def pick(e, f), do: ext(e, f)
    def main() do
      dbg([pick([], fn -> 0 end), pick([], fn -> 1 end)])
    end

Expected on every path: [0, 1].

- interp: "backend dispatch call requires semantic argument 1 value 1: backend generic callable shape ShapeId(14) has no published lane"
- run: artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan, "native attempted to rematerialize generic callable shape ShapeId(14) ... first-class callable values must come from transport publication lanes"
- build: panic at jobs/native.rs:3944, "must be runtime-materializable; value=Absent"

Neighbor to check for a shared cause: fz-afu.14 (a helper-built closure chosen by a case loses its value; "backend value was absent").

Paper first: shrink, answer by hand which lane should carry the closure into ext, find the first difference, fix at the source. Proposal page before building.
title: Two different closures passed through a helper to a shared function fail to compile
